While there may be a slight greening effect due to higher CO2, the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) emphasizes that this benefit is eclipsed by the negative consequences of climate change on food security. Extreme weather events, such as heatwaves and droughts, can drastically reduce crop yields, counteracting any potential gains in photosynthesis. It is crucial to recognize that CO2, while essential for plant growth, is also a powerful greenhouse gas that significantly drives global warming, with human emissions greatly exceeding natural variations in the carbon cycle. A careful approach is necessary to navigate these complexities within our ecosystems, prioritizing emissions reductions and maintaining net-zero integrity.
